speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and what activity triggered it?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis

The history of holding an infant and pain on the thumb/wrist strongly suggests this condition, though I need to confirm if you have pain specifically when moving your thumb away from the palm and if your mother's diagnosis was Rheumatoid Arthritis. Can you describe exactly how the thumb moves when you hold your baby, and do you have any numbness or tingling in your fingers?
